name: Two Sum
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the 0-based indices `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) of two distinct elements whose sum equals the target.

Each test case is two lines on stdin: line 1 is the array `nums` as a JSON array (e.g. `[2,7,11,15]`), and line 2 is the integer `target`. The wrapper parses both lines and calls `solve(nums, target)`. The judge runs each test case independently — your function handles one test case at a time.

Return the index pair as an array `[i, j]`; the wrapper serializes it as a JSON array (e.g. `[0,1]`). Every test case has exactly one valid answer.
output_format: An array `[i, j]` of two 0-based indices into `nums` (with `i < j`) such that `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`, serialized as a JSON array, e.g. `[0,1]`.
hints: Use a hash map: as you scan `nums`, check whether `target - x` was seen earlier.
Indices are 0-based into `nums`, and the smaller index comes first.
Values can be negative and up to ~1e9; prefer 64-bit integers in C++/Go.

languages.wrapper:
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import os
import sys

# bash redirects the answer file onto fd 3 via `3>file`. Move it to a private
# fd and close fd 3 itself so user code can't accidentally write or close it.
# stdin carries this test case's input lines, one per io_schema input field:
# line 0 = nums (int[]), line 1 = target (int). After solve() returns, the
# wrapper writes the JSON-serialized result through the private fd.
_answer_fd = os.dup(3)
os.close(3)

{{.}}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    nums = json.loads(lines[0])
    target = int(lines[1])
    result = solve(nums, target)
    os.write(_answer_fd, json.dumps(result, separators=(",", ":")).encode())
    os.close(_answer_fd)

package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
)

{{.}}

func main() {
	// Move bash-supplied fd 3 to a private fd and close fd 3 so user code
	// can't poke at it. The duplicate is used to deliver the answer below.
	dupFd, _ := syscall.Dup(3)
	_ = syscall.Close(3)
	answer := os.NewFile(uintptr(dupFd), "answer")

	// Two stdin lines for this test case: line 0 = nums, line 1 = target.
	reader := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
	numsLine, _ := reader.ReadString('\n')
	targetLine, _ := reader.ReadString('\n')

	var nums []int64
	_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(strings.TrimSpace(numsLine)), &nums)
	target, _ := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(targetLine), 10, 64)

	result := solve(nums, target)

	payload, _ := json.Marshal(result)
	_, _ = answer.Write(payload)
	_ = answer.Close()
}
